text:
maria-plat: Noticing a big throughput dip in eu-west around 21:12 UTC, p95 up and many worker restarts. dashboards: https://grafana.company/ops/eu-west-throughput  

infra-bot: alert: GPU_OOM_RATE spike on eu-west at 21:11-21:35; impacted_pools=[shared-small,realtime-batches]

aj: Oncall inbound. @nina can you pull kernel-selection and allocator traces for shared-small? We rolled something ~20:58, right?

nina: Yep, kernel-select v2 rolled at 20:58. Runtime logs show a sudden jump to fast-attn for many short requests + allocator slab failures. sample lines:
```
[21:12:03] kernel_select: model=llama-7b variant=q8 fastpath selected (reason=seq_len<256 && batch>1)
[21:12:04] allocator: slab_assign id=3 size=256MB failed->alloc_fallback
[21:12:04] nvml: OOM on GPU-0 pid=4321 mem=6.8GB requested=200MB
[21:12:05] worker: restart pid=4321 reason=OOM
```

kevin: The intent of v2 was to lower latency for medium batches by preferring fast-attn. We underestimated transient reserve behavior when KV-cache is hot + many small concurrent users. Fast-attn peaks memory briefly.

aj: Any evidence of noisy tenants occupying KV and preventing eviction?

maria-plat: Yes — tenant company-x generated a flurry of small reqs at ~21:08-21:26 that kept KV occupancy ~92%. Eviction latency climbed (50ms -> 420ms) so allocators couldn't reclaim quickly.

nina: Quick profiling notes: continuous-batching decreased so more small batches took fastpath; KV evict latency spiked; allocator free-slab fragmentation rose. Result: transient reserved pages + failed slab assigns -> GPU OOMs -> worker restarts.

kevin: Suggested immediate actions: 1) rollback kernel-select v2 on shared-small 2) cap per-tenant concurrency in that pool to 20 3) trigger aggressive KV-sweep to drop occupancy <70% temporarily

aj: Rolling rollback canary now on eu-west-03 and eu-west-05.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollback to kernel-select v1 started (21:24) hosts=[eu-west-03,eu-west-05]

maria-plat: Post-rollback: p95 improved, OOMs dropped. Some worker restarts still as slabs free and KV sweeps finish, but throughput trending up.

nina: Follow-ups for backlog: add gauge for kernel-induced transient-reserve, change heuristic to require KV-occupancy<80% before picking fast-attn, add small-batch scheduler backpressure. Also plan a short aggressive kv-sweep for recovered nodes.

kevin: Agree. Also recommend a quick unit test in our sim harness that models KV-hot scenarios to catch this selection regression.

aj: I'll document timeline and RCA in a short blameless postmortem. Temporary mitigation summary: rollback + tenant cap + kv-sweep; root cause: kernel-selection heuristic + high KV occupancy + noisy small-batch tenant leading to transient memory peaks -> GPU OOM -> worker restarts -> throughput drop.

maria-plat: Marking incident mitigated. Tracking follow-ups in #eng-runtime backlog. :white_check_mark:
